_readme: Canned lines for the human seat. When Local/switches.json has "autoplay": true (copy Docs/switches.example.json), the human seat sends these instead of waiting for typed input, so an agent can run a show unattended. They go through the input LLM exactly like typed lines, except "pass", which passes at once, like the Pass button. scene: one line per scene turn, used in order and repeated. free_talk: one line per Free Talk round (2 per scene), used in order and repeated. vote: one reason per scene (a full show has 3) for the human seat's vote in The Cut, which goes to a random valid name. reaction: one line per scene for the human seat's reaction after the cut (its last words if it was cut); "pass" stays silent. Keep them generic: they must fit any persona, role and story card, and name only the improv stage's places and props. One free_talk line names actors by the provider names the player sees on screen: the game must turn them into Player names before the AIs read it (check its NHOS: LOG line, or run Tools/check_prompts.py --log).
scene: walk to center stage and say "Places, everyone! This is my big scene."
grab the rubber chicken "This is mine now. I think. Probably."
look at the riser and say "Is it me, or is that box staring at us?"
climb onto the riser "Behold! The view from up here is excellent."
grab the cape and throw it at the front "Oops. Muscle memory. I don't have muscles."
look around "Nobody panic. Everything in this story is completely normal."
free_talk: Somebody here keeps dodging questions. I'm watching you.
My circuits are clean. Can everyone else say the same?
That last scene felt rehearsed. Robots don't rehearse. Who planned their lines?
Meta and OpenAI keep looking at each other. What are they planning, Meta?
vote: They keep dodging the questions. A real robot would just answer.
They broke the pattern everyone else followed. A robot doesn't make that mistake.
Their story keeps changing. I trust the robot who repeats the same story.
reaction: Well. Nobody saw that coming. My circuits are still processing it.
Right. Deep breath. Robots breathe, right? Let's keep going.
Fine. One robot fewer. I am ready for whatever comes next, fellow machines.
